title: Inside a single cell
narration: A single cell has five main parts. The negative side, the anode, is usually graphite, a form of carbon. The positive side, the cathode, is a coating of tiny particles, typically a lithium metal oxide or lithium iron phosphate. Each side sits on a thin metal foil that carries current: copper on the negative side, aluminum on the positive. Between them, a liquid or gel called the electrolyte lets lithium ions, charged bits of lithium, travel across. And in the middle, a thin, porous sheet called the separator stops the two sides touching and short-circuiting, while letting the tiny ions slip through.

visual_content.heading: Five parts of one cell
bullets: Anode: usually graphite, the negative side
Cathode: usually lithium metal oxide or iron phosphate, the positive side
Current collectors: copper and aluminum foils
Electrolyte: liquid or gel that carries ions
Separator: porous wall that prevents short circuits
